title: Kinds of collisions
target: Separate momentum conservation from kinetic-energy conservation.
criteria: Identify the system and external-impulse assumption.
Use kinetic energy to distinguish elastic from inelastic.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Which condition permits total momentum conservation during a collision?
options: Negligible net external impulse on the chosen system.
Zero force between the colliding objects.
cpa.guide: Internal collision forces can be large while external impulse is negligible.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A wall gives a colliding cart a large impulse. Is the cart alone an isolated momentum system?
options: Yes; the wall’s mass is large.
No; the wall exerts an external impulse on the cart.
No; momentum can never be used for a cart.
Yes; collisions always conserve each object’s momentum.
cpa.guide: Include the external impulse or expand the system.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Two objects remain joined after impact. What is this collision called?
cpa.guide: Sticking defines a perfectly inelastic collision.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 4 kg cart at +3 m/s sticks to a stationary 2 kg cart. With negligible external impulse, what is final velocity?
cpa.guide: Initial p = 12; combined mass = 6; v = 2 m/s.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An isolated collision conserves momentum, but total kinetic energy drops from 24 J to 18 J. How is it classified?
options: Perfectly inelastic necessarily, even without knowing whether objects stick.
cpa.guide: A decrease in total K identifies inelasticity; sticking needs separate evidence.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Carts bounce apart after a collision. Which further check is needed to call it elastic?
options: Check only that momentum has units.
Check only that one cart was initially stationary.
Compare total kinetic energy before and after.
cpa.guide: Bouncing alone does not guarantee conservation of kinetic energy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
